scope: Proposition 3.4 (A continuous outermost scale) of the manuscript “Bounded scalar curvature and smooth extension of four-dimensional Ricci flow” (preprints/Bounded-scalar-curvature-and-smooth-extension-of-four-dimensional-Ricci-flow-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 351 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 95655c4053c94f2b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 21. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is a fixed small c∗ > 0 such that the following definition detects the unique outermost entry. Choose a bounded continuous ψ : [0, 1] → [0, ∞), zero on [0, c∗] and strictly positive on [2c∗, 1], and set a(t) = sup y∈U l(y, t)ψ l(y, t)2 | Rm |(y, t)  . (3.25) After shrinking U, this supremum is attained in its interior for every late time; it is positive and continuous, and a(t) → 0. For every sequence of late times, scale a(t) and any maximizing point represent the outermost nonflat entry. Every other nonflat entry has scale bounded by a constant times a(t). The constants may be fixed after extracting the sequential tree.
